transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Ortiz (Redwood SE), Elena Garcia (Redwood CSM), Daniel Wu (Aurora Head of Procurement), Monica Perez (Aurora Legal), Arjun Menon (Aurora VP Eng), Lena Park (Aurora Security)

Summary (auto): Quick procurement review: walk through MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations for Dedicated vs Hosted, pricing scenarios, and onboarding/timeline. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send redlined MSA/DPA and SLA/pricing docs; schedule technical pilot.

[00:00] Sophie Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining on a Wednesday, appreciate you making time. quick intros, i'm sophie, i'm the account exec on the aurora deal. Marcus will cover technical SLA bits and dedicated pricing, Elena will run onboarding questions.
[00:15] Daniel Wu: Thanks sophie. quick note, we've got about 6-8 people reviewing legal and security on our side but today it's just me, monica, arjun, and lena. goal is to get procurement and legal comfort so we can sign a PO end of month if things look good.
[00:30] Marcus Ortiz: Hey all, Marcus here, i'll try to keep the deep tech short then leave time for legal questions. just to frame: redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private/vpc deployment. typical procurement asks: data residency, encryption at rest, kms support, and SLA numbers.
[00:45] Monica Perez: Great — starting with the MSA/DPA: we flagged a few items in the draft — indemnity limits, data processing scope in the DPA, sub processor list, and audit rights. we usually ask for SOC2 + ISO attestation and a list of subprocessors.
[00:58] Sophie Chen: absolutely, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation — i'll attach the certs. we also publish an up-to-date sub-processor list; i'll include that link. for indemnity we can discuss typical redwood positions, and there may be some room depending on deal tier.
[01:10] Lena Park: on the security side — do you support customer-managed KMS for private deployments? and what about key management in hosted?
[01:22] Marcus Ortiz: yes — for Private/VPC we integrate with customer KMS/HSM — you can bring your key for at-rest encryption. for hosted, we offer managed keys by default but can support cross-account KMS in certain enterprise setups; i'll share the KMS integration doc.
[01:35] Arjun Menon: latency and cost tradeoffs: our latency SLO is pretty strict for customer-facing flows, sub-200ms P95 on generation is ideal. can dedicated deliver that? and what's the pricing delta vs hosted?
[01:50] Marcus Ortiz: good q — depends on model & sequence length. with reserved dedicated pools pinned to an optimized LLM variant we routinely see P95 in 120-250ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens) on A100/H100 profiles. Pricing: dedicated is commit-based — lower unit cost at scale but requires commit; hosted is pay-as-you-go but higher per-token. i'll put together a couple scenario spreadsheets for your QPS.
[02:05] Daniel Wu: under procurement we need clear SLA numbers — uptime, latency credits, remedies. what SLAs do you offer for hosted vs dedicated?
[02:20] Sophie Chen: currently we have SLA tiers for Dedicated with 99.9%+ uptime commitments and response time targets; hosted has a best-effort SLA for free-tier accounts, and enterprise hosted customers can get stronger SLA commitments. Marcus will enumerate the targets and typical credit structure.
[02:35] Marcus Ortiz: for Dedicated we can commit to 99.9% availability — with credits for drop below that. latency SLOs are a bit different — we publish latency profiles per model and workload; if you require contractual latency SLOs (like 200ms P95), we usually tie that to the dedicated configuration and run an initial benchmark to baseline. credits typically tiered (service credit % based on downtime window). i'll add the sample SLA matrix to the packet.
[02:52] Monica Perez: ok on data residency — we need data to remain in EU for EU customers. can you guarantee region locking and not replicate logs to US infra?
[03:05] Marcus Ortiz: yes, for Private and Dedicated deployed in an EU region we can pin data to region; for Hosted we have region options and policy-based routing — we also have controls for audit logs and retention. i will note that some managed backups may be replicated unless you choose Private on-prem which we can avoid.
[03:20] Lena Park: audit logs — are request/response logs retained? what's the retention window and can you disable SAS logs for certain routes?
[03:32] Elena Garcia: arun — oh sorry, lena — yes we capture request metadata for observability. retention is configurable; enterprise customers can set shorter retention or opt-out for PII sensitive routes. we'll follow up with a config sheet.
[03:46] Arjun Menon: procurement: pricing approvals — we need a few scenarios: pilot (low QPS), mid-scale (10k QPS? no that's wrong, maybe 10 QPS), and production (100s QPS). we'd like to see cost-per-1k tokens for each.
[04:05] Sophie Chen: noted — Marcus will assemble per-mode cost models: hosted pay-as-you-go per token, dedicated reserved pricing with commit tiers, and recommended quantization/ batching settings that affect costs.
[04:20] Daniel Wu: legal asked about breach notification timelines, data subject rights handling, and termination data return. are those covered in the DPA?
[04:35] Monica Perez: and we want explicit language re: subprocessor contract flow-down and ability to audit them if needed.
[04:48] Sophie Chen: yes — standard DPA covers breach notification (we notify within 72 hours of confirmed incident) and we offer data export/return at termination. subprocessor list and flow-downs are part of the DPA and we can provide SOC2 reports on the subprocessors where available.
[05:03] Marcus Ortiz: quick tech note: for pilot we often suggest Hosted for fastest time-to-value; for production with strict data residency / latency needs we recommend Dedicated or Private. dedicated gives you the best balance of predictable latency and unit cost.
[05:18] Arjun Menon: what about fallback behavior — if dedicated capacity is saturated, do you have automatic fallback to hosted or lower-tier models? that's important for graceful degradation.
[05:30] Marcus Ortiz: yes, smart routing can fail over to compatible model variants or regional capacity tiers. we can configure policies: prefer dedicated, fallback to hosted in same region, or deny overflow — whatever suits your compliance posture.
[05:45] Monica Perez: indemnity cap — in our redlines we typically ask for uncapped indemnity for third-party IP claims; is that negotiable?
[05:58] Sophie Chen: we usually have a tiered indemnity cap tied to annual contract value, but for enterprise we can discuss higher limits and carve-outs. i'll flag legal to discuss specific language with you.
[06:10] Daniel Wu: procurement timeline: if legal and security get the certs and redline this week, can you push final MSA by next Monday?
[06:22] Sophie Chen: we can prioritize — we'll send a redlined MSA and DPA today and aim for a finalized version by 2026-03-08 assuming back-and-forth is limited.
[06:35] Lena Park: any certifications around penetration testing? do you provide pen test reports?
[06:48] Marcus Ortiz: we do annual pen tests and we share a summary; for specific clients we can do more detailed reviews under NDA. i'll include the security packet link.
[06:58] Monica Perez: thanks. can you also confirm the escrow/continuity plan if Redwood loses support for a model we depend on?
[07:12] Marcus Ortiz: good point — we have model change policies and recommended migration paths; for mission critical we advise pinning model versions and keeping a fallback model. for long-term continuity we can discuss contractual commitments in the MSA.
[07:30] Daniel Wu: ok let's recap next steps — i want the SLA matrix, pricing scenarios, redlined legal, compliance packet, and we want to schedule a technical pilot benchmark. can we get all that next week?
[07:45] Sophie Chen: yes — recap: sophie will send redlined MSA/DPA + certs today; marcus will send SLA/pricing and pilot plan by Friday 2026-03-06; elena will send onboarding checklist and timeline; customer to confirm internal approvers and procurement timeline by 2026-03-05.
[08:02] Arjun Menon: one more tech question — for KV cache and long context usage, are there policies about retention of cached prompts? we have some IP concerns.
[08:15] Marcus Ortiz: KV cache is ephemeral by default and used for inference performance; we don't persist user prompts beyond configured retention unless you opt into logging. we can set zero-log routes for sensitive contexts.
[08:30] Monica Perez: good. on pricing, any discounts for multi-year commits?
[08:42] Sophie Chen: yes — dedicated reserved capacity gets multi-year discounts and committed spend reduces unit prices; we'll include examples in the pricing scenario doc.
[08:55] Daniel Wu: final — who's the day-to-day Redwood contact during onboarding?
[09:05] Elena Garcia: that's me, elena — i'll be your CSM, i'll coordinate onboarding, tickets, and the initial runbooks.
[09:15] Sophie Chen: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the docs.
[09:22] Meeting end.
